Developmental brain malformations define the disorder; urinary tract defects, including vesicoureteral reflux, occur in 30-79%.
Thallium directly injures peripheral nerves and hair follicles, producing characteristic painful neuropathy and alopecia; gastrointestinal symptoms alone do not establish organ damage.
Inherited red-cell membrane disorder causing hemolysis; gallstones are a separate disease, and pseudohyperkalemia is an ex vivo artifact.
Segmental cutaneous and spinal vascular malformations define the syndrome; muscular and osseous vascular lesions are also defining features. Bladder dysfunction is neurogenic.
Congenital limb malformations involving the ulna, digits and feet.
Mature B-cell lymphoma arising in the small intestine; both hematologic lineage and lymphoma mechanism apply.
Otosclerosis damages the auditory apparatus, causing conductive and sometimes sensorineural hearing loss.
Mitochondrial metabolic disorder with cardiomegaly in 9/9 and anemia in 7/7; hearing loss reported in only one assessed patient is insufficient to establish common involvement.
Malignant tumor arising from the meninges.
Inherited retinal degeneration with visual loss; bronchiectasis occurs in 1/4, below threshold. Situs inversus alone does not imply organ damage.
Histologic subtype of basal cell carcinoma arising in skin.
Isolated inherited intellectual disability is a neurodevelopmental disorder; additional systemic manifestations are excluded by the definition.
Alcohol-associated damage to peripheral somatic and autonomic nerves; other alcohol-related organ diseases are separate conditions.
Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with defining olfactory dysfunction, anosmia in 8/8; hearing impairment in 6/8. Dental abnormalities in 2/8 are below threshold.
Endocrine lesions, cutaneous myxomas/pigmentation and cardiac myxomas are major diagnostic features; cardiac myxomas occurred in 6/11. Schwannomas are less common.
Splitting of retinal layers with loss of visual function.
Umbrella metabolic disorder of sulfur compounds; no additional organ injury is established across most subtypes.
Joint hypermobility syndrome is an arthropathy affecting the locomotor connective tissues.
Unilateral congenital deficiency of the radial portion of a limb.
Hereditary glaucoma causes optic nerve damage and visual loss; systemic findings vary by subtype and are not shared across the group.
Glutathione-related skeletal dysplasia; AV block/arrhythmias occur in 80-99%, cerebellar hypoplasia in 30-79%. Respiratory failure does not establish intrinsic lung damage.
Severe retinal malformations and neurodevelopmental impairment define the deletion syndrome; deafness and immunodeficiency are variably reported without established common frequency.
Rhabdomyosarcoma is a malignant skeletal-muscle-lineage soft-tissue tumor; this concept specifies no single mucosal organ of origin.
Localized malignant cartilage-forming tumor of skeletal or extraskeletal connective tissue; no disseminated organ involvement.
